title: chronological-debt-based-throttling-for-continuous-batcher
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: Continuous batcher starvation and long-tail latency regressions have been observed in mixed KV-heavy workloads where small, low-cost requests repeatedly preempt larger requests, and where stalled requests with large KV pins can hold slots for long periods. Existing priority-decay heuristics reduced some cases but left pathological arrival patterns (bursts of tiny queries or very old requests) that caused tail SLO violations. This PR introduces a chronological debt-based throttling layer in the continuous batching path to (1) prevent starvation of older requests, (2) bound the time a request can hold active reservation without progress, and (3) provide a lightweight admission controller that cooperates with existing batching and KV pin heuristics. Design: - Each request entering the batching queue receives a monotonically increasing sequence timestamp and an initial debt score computed from estimated token work and KV pin cost. Debt accumulates linearly with wall-clock age and is reduced on successful kernel dispatch or when the request is partially serviced via prefix cache hits. - The scheduler computes an effective priority = base_priority + min(debt, debt_cap) - age_penalty_jitter. The debt_cap prevents single old requests from monopolizing throughput. - A soft-ejection timeout is applied per-request: if a request's wall-time in active reservation exceeds soft_timeout_without_progress, it is moved back to the waiting queue and its debt is increased to improve later admission odds; repeated ejections escalate to a hard backoff that defers the request for a short cooldown window to let the batch ecosystem clear. - KV-aware hints: the allocator tags reservations that pin large KV entries; such requests get a scaled debt boost but also a slightly longer soft_timeout to account for unavoidable kernel latency. - Kernel hinting: when multiple requests in a candidate batch share KV pages or overlapping attention windows, we tag the dispatch with a combined_kv_hint to prefer fused kernels (when available) and reduce redundant KV transfers. - Metrics and knobs: new metrics (queue_debt_histogram, eviction_reason_counter, avg_time_to_dispatch_by_age_bucket) and knobs (debt_growth_rate, debt_cap, soft_timeout_ms, hard_backoff_ms, kv_debt_scale) are exposed in the Console and as runtime flags for Dedicated/Private deployments. Implementation notes: - Changes are limited to continuous_batcher/scheduler.go, continuous_batcher/allocator.go, runtime/kv/hints.go and runtime/dispatch/dispatch_coordinator.go. Also added unit and e2e tests under continuous_batcher/test/ and a stress scenario in perf-canary/testvectors/kv_mixed_burst.yaml. - The debt and timeout logic is intentionally lightweight (O(1) per-request bookkeeping) to avoid adding scheduling overhead. - Added deterministic jitter to soft-timeouts to avoid synchronized ejection storms. Testing and results: - Microbenchmarks (local simulated workloads) show 2.8x reduction in 99.9th percentile latency for the mixed KV-small-burst scenario and <3% throughput regression for purely tiny-request workloads when defaults are enabled. - Canary in staging (10% traffic, Dedicated cluster) showed tail latency improvement with no observed increase in error budget; CI runs were adjusted to include the new perf tests. Rollout and migration: - Default knobs are conservative: debt_cap=1.5x, soft_timeout_ms=1200, kv_debt_scale=2.0. We recommend gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with the perf-canary testvector enabled. - No model or API surface changes. Operator notes include guidance for tuning knobs by workload type. Backwards compatibility: no breaking changes to the public API or storage formats.
commits: 3 commits: 1) core: add chronological debt bookkeeping and effective-priority compute; 2) allocator: soft-ejection and hard-backoff logic + KV debt scaling; 3) tests/docs: perf canary, unit tests for ejection paths, Console metrics and knobs
review_thread: Jonas: 'Nice approach. Two concerns: 1) the debt growth params could starve tiny requests in extreme old-request scenarios; 2) how will this interact with the current slot-reservation preemption?' Asha: 'Added per-age-bucket caps and deterministic jitter to mitigate synchronized starvation; revised tests to include tiny-only workloads. Added note about preemption: soft-ejection returns reservation and does not preempt kernel once dispatch begins.' Priya: 'Please add a dashboard for eviction_reason_counter and an alert for sustained hard-backoff rates' -> Asha: 'Added dash and alert in docs and Console defaults; tweaked default debt_cap down from 2.0 to 1.5.' Markus: 'nit: move jitter code to util/time for reuse' -> addressed. Final approval from Jonas and Priya after CI perf runs passed.
release_notes: Introduce chronological debt-based throttling for continuous batcher: improves tail latency in mixed KV and tiny-request workloads by bounding request holding time and prioritizing older stalled work. Exposes tuning knobs for debt growth, caps, and timeouts. Ships metrics for debugging ejection/backoff behavior.
